'''Uta Fritze-von Alvensleben''' is a German astrophysicist awarded the [[German Physical Society]]'s [[Hertha Sponer|Hertha-Sponer]] prize in 2003 for her work on the evolution of galaxies.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Presseinformationen - Georg-August-Universität Göttingen|url=http://www.uni-goettingen.de/de/3240.html?archive=true&archive_source=presse&archive_id=968|last=Öffentlichkeitsarbeit|first=Georg-August-Universität Göttingen-|website=www.uni-goettingen.de|language=de|access-date=2020-05-17}}</ref>

== Career ==
Fritze-von Alvensleben was born in [[Munich]] and studied physics and philosophy at the [[University of Göttingen|Georg-August University]] in [[Göttingen]]. During her studies there, she visited the [[Grenoble Alpes University|Grenoble Alps University]] in France, and at [[CERN]] in [[Geneva]], Switzerland. She then completed her studies at the University of Göttingen in 1982 with a diploma. She finished her PhD in 1989 in [[astrophysics]] with studies about comparing [[Spectrophotometry|spectrophotometric]] models of nearby galaxies with experimental redshift survey results.<ref>{{Cite book|last=Meylan|first=Georges|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Md_tCAAAQBAJ&q=uta+fritze+phd&pg=PA84|title=QSO Absorption Lines: Proceedings of the ESO Workshop Held at Garching, Germany, 21–24 November 1994|date=2013-11-11|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=978-3-540-49458-4|location=|pages=82|language=en}}</ref> In January 2001 she [[Habilitation|habilitated]] at the [[University of Göttingen]] with a study on the evolution of galaxies on cosmological time scales at the [[Göttingen Observatory]]. 

In 2005, she became a member of the ''Observing Program Committee'' for the [[European Southern Observatory]] (ESO). She was jointly responsible for assigning telescope time to different scientists for each of the eight large ESO telescopes in Chile.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Presseinformationen - Georg-August-Universität Göttingen|url=http://www.uni-goettingen.de/de/3240.html?archive=true&archive_source=presse&archive_id=1908|last=Öffentlichkeitsarbeit|first=Georg-August-Universität Göttingen-|website=www.uni-goettingen.de|language=de|access-date=2020-05-17}}</ref>

After this, she researched and taught at the [[University of Hertfordshire]] as part of GALEV (Galaxy Evolution Group) at the ''Center for Astrophysics Research''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Homepage of Galaxy Evolution (Galev) Group, Centre for Astrophysics Research, University of Hertfordshire|url=http://members.galev.org/ufritze/|website=members.galev.org|access-date=2020-05-17}}</ref>

Fritze-von Alvensleben has been working at the [[University of Göttingen]] since 2008 where she has worked on the Göttingen Evolutionary Synthesis Code for the unified spectral, chemical and cosmological evolution of galaxies.

She was awarded the [[Hertha Sponer|Hertha-Sponer]] prize in 2003 from the [[German Physical Society]] for her investigations ''into the spectral and chemical evolution of galaxies on cosmological time scales, particularly under the influence of interactions''. The award ceremony took place during the 67th Physics Conference in March 2003 in [[Hanover]], Germany.<ref name=":0" />

She remains a member of the [[International Astronomical Union]] and has been a member of the group's Division J Galaxies and Cosmology.<ref>{{Cite web|title=International Astronomical Union {{!}} IAU|url=https://www.iau.org/administration/membership/individual/1001/|website=www.iau.org|access-date=2020-05-17}}</ref>

== Selected publications ==

* Contardo, Gertrud, Matthias Steinmetz, and Uta Fritze-von Alvensleben. "Photometric evolution of galaxies in cosmological scenarios." ''The Astrophysical Journal'' 507, no. 2 (1998): 497.
* Alloin, Danielle, Carme Gallart, Emmanuel Fleurence, Emanuela Pompei, Daniel Raimann, Uta Fritze-Von Alvensleben, and Sukyoung Yi. "Deriving star formation histories: Evolutionary or population synthesis codes versus color-magnitude diagrams." ''Astrophysics and space science'' 281 (2002): 109-113.
* Weilbacher, Peter M., Uta Fritze-von Alvensleben, and P-A. Duc. "Optical and NIR investigation of a sample of tidal dwarf candidates." ''Astrophysics and space science'' 284 (2003): 639-642.
* Bicker, Jens, Uta Fritze-von Alvensleben, and K. J. Fricke. "Evolutionary synthesis models for galaxy transformation in clusters." ''Astrophysics and space science'' 284, no. 2 (2003): 463-466.
